Requires option SRAUTOSEN.
The search condition must be set to FAST.
The number of channels must be set to 1.
The nibble count must be set to 6.
commands.arguments:
<Qstring> is the Fast Channel 1 fast message counter binary value on which
to trigger.

examples.description: sets the Fast Channel 1 fast message counter value to "don't care." TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:FAST:COUNTER:VALUE? might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:FAST:COUNTER:VALUE "00001111" to indicate the Fast Channel 1 fast message counter binary value on which to trigger is 00001111.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the binary fast message counter value to be used when triggering on a SENT bus signal.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This command sets or queries the binary fast message inverted nibble value to be used when triggering on a SENT bus signal. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions:
Requires option SRAUTOSEN.
The search condition must be set to FAST.
The number of channels must be set to 1.
The nibble count must be set to 6.
commands.arguments: <Qstring> is the Fast Channel 1 inverted nibble binary value on which to trigger.

examples.description: sets the Fast Channel 1 secure inverted nibble value to "don't care." TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:FAST:INVERTNIBBLE:VALUE? might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:FAST:INVERTNIBBLE:VALUE "1111" to indicate a binary value of 1111.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the binary fast message inverted nibble value to be used when triggering on a SENT bus signal.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This command sets or queries the binary status value to be used when triggering on a SENT bus signal. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions:
Requires option SRAUTOSEN.
The search trigger condition must be set to FAST.
commands.arguments: <Qstring> is the binary status value on which to trigger.

examples.description: sets the binary status trigger value to XXXX.
might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:FAST:STATUS:VALUE "1010" to indicate a binary trigger value is 1010.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the binary status value to be used when triggering on a SENT bus signal.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This command sets or queries the qualifier to be used when triggering on SENT pause pulses. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions: Requires option SRAUTOSEN. The SENT bus trigger condition must be set to PAUSE.
commands.arguments:
EQUal sets the qualifier as Equal.
INrange sets the qualifier to in range.
LESSEQual sets the qualifier as Less Than or Equal to.
LESSThan sets the qualifier as Less Than.
MOREEQual sets the qualifier as More Than or Equal to.
MOREThan sets the qualifier as More Than.
OUTrange sets the qualifier to out of range.
UNEQual sets the qualifier as Unequal.

examples.description: sets the pause pulse qualifier trigger to not equal for bus 2.
might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:PAUSE:QUALIFIER INRANGE to indicate that the pause pulse qualifier is set to trigger inside the range of ticks low and ticks high on bus 1.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the qualifier to be used when triggering on SENT pause pulses.
commands.name: QUALifier

params.name: value
params.description: One of: EQual, UNEQual, LESSthan, MOREthan, LESSEQual, MOREEQual, Inrange, OUTrange

commands.description: This command sets or queries the high binary Slow channel data value to use when triggering on a SENT bus signal. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions:
Requires option SRAUTOSEN.
The SENT bus trigger condition must be set to SLOW.
commands.arguments: <Qstring> sets the binary Slow channel data value.

examples.description: sets the Slow data high value to "don't care." TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:SLOW:DATA:HIVALUE? might return TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:SLOW:DATA:HIVALUE "11110001", to indicate triggering on Slow data values that match 11110001.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the high binary Slow channel data value to use when triggering on a SENT bus signal.
commands.name: HIVALue

commands.description: This command sets or queries the binary identifier value to use when triggering on a SENT bus signal. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions:
Requires option SRAUTOSEN
The SENT bus trigger condition must be set to SLOW.
commands.arguments:
EQUal specifies the qualifier as Equal.
UNEQual specifies the qualifier as Not Equal to.
LESSthan specifies the qualifier as Less Than.
MOREthan specifies the qualifier as More Than. LESSEQual specifies the qualifier as Less Than or Equal to.
MOREEQual specifies the qualifier as More Than or Equal to.
INRange sets the qualifier to inside a range.
OUTRange sets the qualifier to outside a range.

examples.description: sets the slow channel data qualifier to less than or equal for bus 2.
might return :TRIGger:A:BUS:B5:SENT:SLOW:DATA:QUALIFIER EQUAL to indicate that the slow channel data qualifier is set to equal on bus 5.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the binary identifier value to use when triggering on a SENT bus signal.
commands.name: QUALifier

params.name: value
params.description: One of: EQual, UNEQual, LESSthan, MOREthan, LESSEQual, MOREEQual, INRange, OUTRange

commands.description: This command sets or queries the binary slow channel value to use when triggering on a SENT bus signal. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions:
Requires option SRAUTOSEN
The SENT bus trigger condition must be set to SLOW.
commands.arguments: <Qstring> is the binary slow channel data value.

examples.description: sets the slow data value to "don't care" for bus 2.
might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B4:SENT:SLOW:DATA:VALUE "XXXX1111", to indicate triggering on slow data values that match XXXX1111 on bus 4.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the binary slow channel value to use when triggering on a SENT bus signal.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This command sets or queries the qualifier to use when triggering on SENT slow packet bus data. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.conditions:
Requires option SRAUTOSEN
The SENT bus trigger condition must be set to SLOW.
commands.arguments: <Qstring> is the binary identifier value.

examples.description: sets the identifier value to "don't care" for bus 3.
might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SENT:SLOW:IDENTIFIER:VALUE "0001" to indicate the slow channel identifier is set to 0001 on bus 1.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the qualifier to use when triggering on SENT slow packet bus data.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This command specifies the trigger condition for a SPI trigger. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.arguments:
SS specifies the Slave Selection condition.
STARTofframe is applicable when BUS:B<x>:SPI:FRAMING is set to
IDLEtime. When the trigger condition is set to STARTofframe, the instrument
triggers on the first SPI clock after an idle time when there are no clocks.
DATa sets the trigger condition to Master-In Slave-Out and Master-Out Slave-In.
commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the trigger condition for a SPI trigger.
commands.name: CONDition

commands.description: This command specifies the length of the data string to be used for a SPI trigger if the trigger condition is DATa. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.arguments: <NR1> is the length of the data string in bytes.

examples.description: sets the data size to 1 byte.
might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SPI:DATA:SIZE 1 indicating the data size is 1 byte.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the length of the data string to be used for a SPI trigger if the trigger condition is DATa.
commands.name: SIZe

commands.description: This command specifies the binary data string used for SPI triggering if the trigger condition is DATA. B<x> is the specified bus number.
commands.arguments:
<QString> specifies the data value in the specified valid format. The valid
characters are 0, 1, and X for binary format.

examples.description: sets the data value to 11011010.
might return :TRIGGER:A:BUS:B1:SPI:DATA:VALUE "XXXXXXXX" indicating the data value is XXXXXXXX.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the binary data string used for SPI triggering if the trigger condition is DATA.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This command sets or queries the source bus for a bus trigger.
commands.arguments: B<x> sets the selected source to the bus.

examples.description: sets the selected source for the bus trigger to Bus 2.
might return TRIGGER:A:BUS:SOURCE B1, indicating that the selected source for the bus trigger is set to Bus 1.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the source bus for a bus trigger.
commands.name: SOUrce

commands.description: This command sets or queries the type of coupling for the edge trigger. This command is equivalent to selecting Edge from the Trigger Type drop-down in the Trigger setup context menu, and choosing from the Coupling drop-down list.
commands.arguments:
DC selects DC trigger coupling, which passes all input signals to the trigger
circuitry.
HFRej coupling attenuates signals above 50 kHz before passing the signals to the
trigger circuitry.
LFRej coupling attenuates signals below 80 kHz before passing the signals to the
trigger circuitry.
NOISErej coupling provides stable triggering by increasing the trigger hysteresis.
Increased hysteresis reduces the trigger sensitivity to noise but can require greater
trigger signal amplitude.

examples.description: sets the A edge trigger coupling to DC.
might return :TRIGGER:A:EDGE:COUPLING DC, indicating that the A edge trigger coupling is set to DC.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the type of coupling for the edge trigger.
commands.name: COUPling

params.name: value
params.description: One of: DC, HFRej, LFRej, NOISErej

commands.description: This command sets or queries the slope for the edge trigger. This command is equivalent to selecting Edge from the Trigger Type drop-down in the Trigger setup context menu, and then choosing the desired Slope. This command is also equivalent to pressing the front-panel Slope button.
commands.arguments:
RISe specifies to trigger on the rising or positive edge of a signal.
FALL specifies to trigger on the falling or negative edge of a signal.
EITHER specifies to trigger on either the rising or falling edge of a signal.

examples.description: sets the A edge trigger slope to positive, which triggers on the rising edge of the signal.
might return :TRIGGER:A:EDGE:SLOPE FALL, indicating that the A edge trigger slope is negative.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the slope for the edge trigger.
commands.name: SLOpe

commands.description: This command sets or queries the source for the edge trigger. For instruments that have an Auxiliary Input, AUXiliary can be selected as trigger source.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies an analog channel as the edge trigger source.
DCH<x>_D<x> specifies a digital channel as the edge trigger source. The
supported digital channel value is 1. The supported digital bit values are 0 to 15.
INTernal specifies a internal edge trigger source.
AUXiliary specifies the Auxiliary Input.

examples.description: sets the A edge trigger source to input channel 2.
might return :TRIGGER:A:EDGE:SOURCE CH1, indicating that the A edge trigger source is set to input channel 1.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the source for the edge trigger.
commands.name: SOUrce

params.name: value
params.description: One of: CH<x>, DCH<x>_D<x>, INTernal, AUXiliary

commands.description: This command sets or queries the A trigger holdoff time. This command is equivalent to selecting Mode & Holdoff from the Trig menu, selecting Time, and then setting the desired Holdoff Time.
commands.arguments:
<NR3> specifies the holdoff time in seconds. The range is from 0 seconds through
10 seconds.

examples.description: sets the A trigger holdoff time to 10 s.
might return :TRIGGER:A:HOLDOFFTIME 1.2000E-06, indicating that the A trigger holdoff time is set to 1.2 �s.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the A trigger holdoff time.
commands.name: TIMe

commands.description: This command sets or queries the CH<x> trigger level for an Edge, Pulse Width, Runt or Rise/Fall (Transition and Slew Rate) trigger when triggering on an analog channel waveform. Each channel can have an independent trigger level. The <x> is the channel number.
commands.arguments: <NR3> specifies the trigger level in user units (usually volts).

examples.description: sets the A trigger level for Channel 1 to 1.5 V.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LEVEL:CH2 1.3000E+00, indicating that the A trigger level for Channel 2 is set to 1.3 V.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the CH<x> trigger level for an Edge, Pulse Width, Runt or Rise/Fall (Transition and Slew Rate) trigger when triggering on an analog channel waveform.
commands.name: CH<x>

commands.description: This command specifies or queries the Logic trigger delta time value. The time value is used as part of the Logic trigger condition to determine if the duration of a logic pattern meets the specified time constraints.
commands.arguments: <NR3> the Logic trigger delta time value.

examples.description: sets the delta time to 4.5 ns.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:DELTATIME 4.0E-9 indicating the delta time is set to 4 ns.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies or queries the Logic trigger delta time value.
commands.name: DELTatime

commands.description: This command sets or queries the logical combination of the input channels for logic triggers. This command is equivalent to selecting Logic for the Trigger Type, and setting or viewing the Define Logic.
commands.arguments:
AND specifies to trigger if all conditions are true.
NANd specifies to trigger if any of the conditions are false.
NOR specifies to trigger if all conditions are false.
OR specifies to trigger if any of the conditions are true.

examples.description: sets the logical combination of channels to be true when all conditions are true.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:FUNCTION NAND, indicating that the instrument will trigger if the AND logic conditions are false.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the logical combination of the input channels for logic triggers.
commands.name: FUNCtion

params.name: value
params.description: One of: AND, NANd, NOR, OR

commands.description: This command specifies the channel to use as the clock source for logic trigger.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies an analog channel as the clock source. Number of channels
depends on instrument configuration.
DCH<x>_D<x> specifies a digital channel as the clock source. The supported
digital channel value is 1. The supported digital bit values are 0 to 15.

examples.description: sets the clock source to channel 3.
might return TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:INPUT:CLOCK:SOURCE CH3 indicating the clock source is set to channel 3.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the channel to use as the clock source for logic trigger.
commands.name: SOUrce

commands.description: This command sets or queries the polarity for the clock channel when Use Clock Edge is set to Yes for Logic trigger type.
commands.arguments:
NEGative specifies negative polarity.
POSITIVe specifies positive polarity.
EITher specifies either polarity.

examples.description: sets the polarity to either positive or negative.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:POLARITY POSITIVE indicating the polarity is set to positive.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the polarity for the clock channel when Use Clock Edge is set to Yes for Logic trigger type.
commands.name: POLarity

commands.description: This command specifies whether or not Logic trigger type uses clock source.
commands.arguments:
ON|1 specifies that logic trigger type uses clock source.
OFF|0 specifies that logic trigger type does not use clock source.
<NR1> = 0 specifies that logic trigger type does not use clock source; any other
value uses clock source.

examples.description: specifies that the clock edge will not be used.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:USECLOCKEDGE 1 indicating that the clock edge will be used.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies whether or not Logic trigger type uses clock source.
commands.name: USECLockedge

commands.description: This command sets or queries the condition for generating an A or B logic trigger with respect to the defined input pattern. This command is equivalent to selecting Logic for Trigger Type, Use Clock Edge to No, and choosing a trigger condition from the Logic Pattern drop-down list.
commands.arguments:
TRUe triggers on an input pattern that is true.
FALSe triggers on an input pattern that is false.
MOREthan triggers on an input pattern that is true for a time period greater than a
user defined Time Limit (DELTatime) value.
LESSthan triggers on an input pattern that is true for a time period less than a
user defined Time Limit (DELTatime) value.
EQual triggers on an input pattern that is true for a time period equal to a user
defined Time Limit (DELTatime) value.
UNEQual triggers on an input pattern that is true for a time period not equal to a
user defined Time Limit (DELTatime) value.

examples.description: specifies triggering when the input pattern is true for a time period equal to a user defined Time Limit value.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:WHEN TRUE indicating a trigger when the logic is true.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the condition for generating an A or B logic trigger with respect to the defined input pattern.
commands.name: WHEn

params.name: value
params.description: One of: TRUe, FALSe, MOREThan, LESSThan, EQual, UNEQual

commands.description: This command sets or queries the Logic Pattern for the specified channel. This command is used along with the Define Logic choice (LOGIc:FUNCtion) to determine when the logic trigger occurs.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies the channel.
HIGH specifies triggering when the pattern is high.
LOW specifies triggering when the pattern is low.
X specifies triggering when the pattern is high or low.

examples.description: sets the triggering logic to when pattern is high.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:LOGICPATTERN:CH2 X indicating the state can be high or low.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the Logic Pattern for the specified channel.
commands.name: CH<x>

commands.description: This command sets or queries the Logic Pattern for the specified digital channel. This command is used along with the Define Logic choice (LOGIc:FUNCtion) to determine when the logic trigger occurs.
commands.arguments:
DCH<x>_D<x> specifies the digital channel. The supported digital channel value
is 1. The supported digital bits values are 0 to 15.
HIGH specifies triggering when the pattern is high.
LOW specifies triggering when the pattern is low.
X specifies triggering when the pattern is high or low.

examples.description: sets the triggering logic to when pattern is high.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:LOGICPATTERN:DCH1_D1 X indicating the state can be high or low.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the Logic Pattern for the specified digital channel.
commands.name: DCH<x>_D<x>

commands.description: This command sets or queries the A or B lower trigger level threshold for the channel, specified by x.
commands.arguments: <NR3> specifies the threshold voltage in user units.

examples.description: sets the A trigger threshold voltage for Channel 2 to 1.3 V.
might return TRIGGER:A:LOWERTHRESHOLD:CH3 1.2000E+00, indicating that the A trigger threshold voltage for Channel 3 is 1.2 V.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the A or B lower trigger level threshold for the channel, specified by x.
commands.name: CH<x>

commands.description: This command sets or queries the A trigger mode. This command is equivalent to pushing the Mode button on the front panel.
commands.arguments:
AUTO generates a trigger if one is not detected within a specified time period.
NORMal waits for a valid trigger event.

examples.description: sets the trigger mode to normal.
might return TRIGGER:A:MODE AUTO, indicating that the trigger mode is auto.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the A trigger mode.
commands.name: MODe

commands.description: This command specifies the upper limit to use, in seconds, when triggering on detection of a pulse whose duration is inside or outside a range of two values. (Use TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit to specify the lower value of the range.)
commands.arguments: <NR3> is a floating point number that represents the higher value of the range.

examples.description: sets the high limit to 110.0 ns.
might return TRIGGER:A:PULSEWIDTH:HIGHLIMIT 178.88000E-9 indicates the high limit is set to 178.88 ns.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the upper limit to use, in seconds, when triggering on detection of a pulse whose duration is inside or outside a range of two values.
commands.name: HIGHLimit

commands.description: This command specifies the lower limit to use, in seconds, when triggering on detection of a pulse whose duration is inside or outside a range of two values. (Use TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:HIGHLimit to specify the upper limit of the range.) This command also specifies the single limit to use, in seconds, when triggering on detection of a pulse whose duration is less than, greater than, equal to, or not equal to this time limit.
commands.arguments: <NR3> is a floating point number that represents the lower value of the range.

examples.description: sets the low limit to 100.0 ns.
might return TRIGGER:A:PULSEWIDTH:LOWLIMIT 77.7600E-9 indicating the low limit is set to 77.76 ns.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the lower limit to use, in seconds, when triggering on detection of a pulse whose duration is inside or outside a range of two values.
commands.name: LOWLimit

commands.description: This command specifies the polarity for a pulse width trigger.
commands.arguments:
NEGative specifies a negative pulse.
POSitive specifies a positive pulse.

examples.description: sets the pulse polarity to negative.
might return TRIGGER:A:WIDTH:POLARITY POSITIVE indicating a positive pulse.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the polarity for a pulse width trigger.
commands.name: POLarity

commands.description: This command specifies the source waveform for a pulse width trigger.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies an analog input channel as the pulse-width trigger source.
DCH<x>_D<x> specifies an digital input channel as the pulse-width trigger source.
The supported digital channel value is 1. The supported digital bit values are
0 to 15.

examples.description: sets channel 1 as the pulse width source.
might return :TRIGGER:A:PULSEWIDTH:SOURCE CH1 indicating that channel 1 is the pulse width trigger source.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the source waveform for a pulse width trigger.
commands.name: SOUrce

commands.description: This command specifies to trigger when a pulse is detected with a width (duration) that is less than, greater than, equal to, or unequal to a specified value (set using TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit), OR whose width falls outside of or within a specified range of two values (set using TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit and TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:HIGHLimit).
commands.arguments:
LESSthan causes a trigger when a pulse is detected with a width less than the
time set by the TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit command.
MOREthan causes a trigger when a pulse is detected with a width greater than the
time set by the TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit command.
EQual causes a trigger when a pulse is detected with a width equal to the time
period specified in TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit within a �5% tolerance.
UNEQual causes a trigger when a pulse is detected with a width
greater than or less than (but not equal) the time period specified in
TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit within a �5% tolerance.
WIThin causes a trigger when a pulse is detected that is within a range set by
two values.
OUTside causes a trigger when a pulse is detected that is outside of a range set
by two values.

examples.description: :TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:WHEn LESSthan causes the instrument to trigger when a pulse is detected that is shorter than the time specified by TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit.
might return TRIGGER:A:PULSEWIDTH:WHEN GREATER THAN 2.0000E-9, indicating that a trigger is generated when a pulse is detected greater than 2 ns.
might return TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:WHEn MOREthan indicating that a trigger is generated when a pulse is detected that is greater than the time specified by TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies to trigger when a pulse is detected with a width (duration) that is less than, greater than, equal to, or unequal to a specified value (set using TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit), OR whose width falls outside of or within a specified range of two values (set using TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:LOWLimit and TRIGger:A:PULSEWidth:HIGHLimit).
commands.name: WHEn

params.name: value
params.description: One of: LESSthan, MOREthan, EQual, UNEQual, WIThin, OUTside

commands.description: This command specifies the polarity for the runt trigger.
commands.arguments:
POSitive indicates that the rising edge crosses the low threshold and the falling
edge recrosses the low threshold without either edge ever crossing the high
threshold.
NEGative indicates that the falling edge crosses the high threshold and the
rising edge recrosses the high threshold without either edge ever crossing the
low threshold.
EITher triggers on a runt of either polarity.

examples.description: specifies that the polarity of the A pulse runt trigger is negative.
might return :TRIGGER:A:RUNT:POLARITY POSITIVE indicating that the polarity of the A pulse runt trigger is positive.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the polarity for the runt trigger.
commands.name: POLarity

commands.description: This command specifies the source waveform for the runt trigger. NOTE. Digital channels are not supported as runt trigger sources.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies the analog channel number to use as the source waveform for the
runt trigger. To specify the threshold levels when using CH<x> as the source, use
TRIGger:A:LOWerthreshold:CH<x> and TRIGger:A:UPPerthreshold:CH<x>.

examples.description: sets channel 4 as the trigger source.
might return :TRIGGER:A:RUNT:SOURCE CH2 indicating that channel 2 is the trigger source.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the source waveform for the runt trigger.
commands.name: SOUrce

commands.description: This command specifies the type of pulse width the trigger checks for when it detects a runt.
commands.arguments:
OCCURS sets the instrument to trigger if a runt signal of any detectable width
occurs.
LESSthan sets the instrument to trigger if the a runt pulse is detected with width
less than the time set by the TRIGger:A:RUNT:WIDth command.
MOREthan sets the instrument to trigger if the a runt pulse is detected with width
greater than the time set by the TRIGger:A:RUNT:WIDth command.
EQual sets the instrument to trigger if a runt pulse is detected with width equal to
the time period specified in TRIGger:A:RUNT:WIDth within a �5% tolerance.
UNEQual sets the instrument to trigger if a runt pulse is detected with width
greater than or less than (but not equal to) the time period specified in
TRIGger:A:RUNT:WIDth within a �5% tolerance.

examples.description: sets the runt trigger to occur when the instrument detects a runt in a pulse wider than the specified width.
might return :TRIGGER:A:PULSE:RUNT:WHEN OCCURS indicating that a runt trigger will occur if the instrument detects a runt of any detectable width.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the type of pulse width the trigger checks for when it detects a runt.
commands.name: WHEn

params.name: value
params.description: One of: LESSthan, MOREthan, EQual, UNEQual, OCCURS

commands.description: This command specifies the width, in seconds, for a runt trigger.
commands.arguments: <NR3> is a floating point number that specifies the minimum width, in seconds.

examples.description: sets the minimum width of the pulse runt trigger to 15 �s.
might return :TRIGGER:A:PULSE:RUNT:WIDTH 2.0000E-09 indicating that the minimum width of a pulse runt trigger is 2 ns.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the width, in seconds, for a runt trigger.
commands.name: WIDth

commands.description: This command specifies the clock edge polarity for setup and hold triggering.
commands.arguments:
FALL specifies polarity as the clock falling edge.
RISe specifies polarity as the clock rising edge.

examples.description: specifies the polarity as the clock rising edge.
might return :TRIGGER:A:SETHOLD:CLOCK:EDGE RISE indicating that polarity is specified as the clock rising edge.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the clock edge polarity for setup and hold triggering.
commands.name: EDGE

commands.description: This command specifies the clock source for the setup and hold triggering. You cannot specify the same source for both clock and data.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies the analog channel to use as the clock source waveform.
DCH<x>_D<x> specifies the digital channel to use as the clock source waveform.
The supported digital channel value is 1. The supported digital bit values are
0 to 15.

examples.description: specifies channel 1 as the clock source for a setup and hold trigger operation.
might return :TRIGGER:A:SETHOLD:CLOCK:SOURCE CH4 indicating that channel 4 is the clock source for a setup and hold trigger operation.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the clock source for the setup and hold triggering.
commands.name: SOUrce

commands.description: This command specifies the hold time for setup and hold violation triggering. This command is equivalent to selecting Setup/Hold Setup from the Trig menu and then setting the desired Hold Time.
commands.arguments:
<NR3> is a floating point number that specifies the hold time setting, in seconds.
Positive values for hold time occur after the clock edge. Negative values occur
before the clock edge.

examples.description: sets the hold time for the setup and hold trigger to 3 ms.
might return :TRIGGER:A:SETHOLD:HOLDTIME 2.0000E-09 indicating that the current hold time for the setup and hold trigger is 2 ns.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the hold time for setup and hold violation triggering.
commands.name: HOLDTime

commands.description: This command specifies the setup time for setup and hold violation triggering. This command is equivalent to selecting Setup/Hold Setup from the Trig menu and then setting the desired Setup Time.
commands.arguments:
<NR3> is a floating point number that specifies the setup time for setup and hold
violation triggering.

examples.description: specifies that the current setup time for setup and hold trigger is 3 �s.
might return :TRIGGER:A:LOGIC:SETHOLD:SETTIME 2.0000E-09 indicating that the current setup time for setup and hold trigger is 2 ns.

commands.shortDescription: This command specifies the setup time for setup and hold violation triggering.
commands.name: SETTime

commands.description: When triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type, this commands specifies the polarity to be used.
commands.arguments:
STAYSHigh. Trigger when the signal stays high during the timeout time specified
by the command TRIGger:A:TIMEOut:TIMe.
STAYSLow. Trigger when the signal stays low during the timeout time specified
by the command TRIGger:A:TIMEOut:TIMe.
EITher. Trigger when the signal is either high or low during the timeout time
specified by the command TRIGger:A:TIMEOut:TIMe.

examples.description: specifies to trigger when the signal stays high during the timeout time when triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type.
might return EITHER, indicating that the signal stays either high or low during the timeout time.

commands.shortDescription: When triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type, this commands specifies the polarity to be used.
commands.name: POLarity

commands.description: When triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type, this command specifies the source. The available sources are live channels and digital channels. The default is channel 1. The timeout trigger type is selected using TRIGger:A:TYPe TIMEOut.
commands.arguments:
CH<x> specifies an analog channel as the timeout trigger source.
DCH<x>_D<x> specifies a digital channel as the timeout trigger source. The
supported digital channel value is 1. The supported digital bit values are 0 to 15.

examples.description: specifies to use channel 4 as the source for the timeout trigger.
might return CH1, indicating that channel 1 has been set as the source for the timeout trigger.

commands.shortDescription: When triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type, this command specifies the source.
commands.name: SOUrce

commands.description: When triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type, this command specifies the timeout time, in seconds. This command is equivalent to selecting Timeout from the Trig menu and setting a value for Time Limit. The timeout trigger type is selected using TRIGger:A:TYPe TIMEOut
commands.arguments: <NR3> is a floating point number that specifies the timeout time, in seconds.

examples.description: :TRIGger:A:TIMEOut:TIMe 4.0E-9 specifies the timeout time of 4.0 nsec. :TRIGger:A:TIMEOut:TIMe? might return 8.0000E-9.

commands.shortDescription: When triggering using the TIMEOut trigger type, this command specifies the timeout time, in seconds.
commands.name: TIMe

commands.description: This command sets or queries the type of A trigger.
syntax: TRIGger:A:TYPe {EDGE| WIDth| RISE| FALL| TIMEOut| RUNt| LOGIc| SETHold| BUS} TRIGger:A:TYPe?
commands.arguments:
EDGE is a normal trigger. A trigger event occurs when a signal passes through
a specified voltage level in a specified direction and is controlled by the
TRIGger:A:EDGE commands.
WIDth specifies that the trigger occurs when a pulse with a specified width is
found.
RISE specifies that the trigger occurs when a pulse with a specified rise is found.
FALL specifies that the trigger occurs when a pulse with a specified fall is found.
TIMEOut specifies that a trigger occurs when a pulse with the specified timeout
is found.
RUNt specifies that a trigger occurs when a pulse with the specified parameters
is found.
LOGIc specifies that a trigger occurs when specified conditions are met and is
controlled by the TRIGger:A:LOGIc commands.
SETHold specifies that a trigger occurs when a signal is found that meets the
setup and hold parameters.
BUS specifies that a trigger occurs when a signal is found that meets the specified
bus setup parameters.

examples.description: sets the A trigger type to EDGE.
might return :TRIGGER:A:TYPE RUNT indicating that the A trigger type is a runt trigger.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the type of A trigger.
commands.name: TYPe

params.name: value
params.description: One of: EDGE, WIDth, RISE, FALL, TIMEOut, RUNt, LOGIc, SETHold, BUS

commands.description: This command sets or queries the specified channel upper trigger level. The CH<x> range is 1 to 4 and depends on the number of analog channels on your instrument.
commands.arguments: <NR3> specifies the trigger level in user units (usually volts).

examples.description: sets the A trigger level for Channel 1 to 1.3 V level.
might return TRIGGER:A:UPPERTHRESHOLD:CH2 1.3000E+00, indicating that the A trigger level for Channel 2 is set to 1.3 V.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the specified channel upper trigger level.
commands.name: CH<x>

commands.description: This command sets or queries the Auxiliary Input voltage level to use for an edge trigger.
commands.arguments:
<NR3> is trigger level in Volts.
ECL sets trigger level to -1.3 Volts.
TTL sets trigger level to 1.4 Volts.

examples.description: sets trigger level for the Auxiliary Input to 1.2 Volts.

commands.returns: <NR3> is trigger level in Volts.
commands.shortDescription: This command sets or queries the Auxiliary Input voltage level to use for an edge trigger.
commands.name: AUXLevel

commands.description: This command enables or disables user-defined trigger hysteresis.
commands.arguments:
ON enables user-defined trigger hysteresis.
OFF disables user-defined trigger hysteresis.
1 enables user-defined trigger hysteresis.
0 disables user-defined trigger hysteresis.

examples.description: enables user-defined trigger hysteresis.
might return TRIGger:HYSTeresis:USER:STATe 0, indicating that the user-defined trigger hysteresis is disabled.

commands.shortDescription: This command enables or disables user-defined trigger hysteresis.
commands.name: STATe

commands.description: This command sets or returns the height of the user-defined trigger hysteresis zone in volts.
commands.arguments: <NR1> sets the height of the hysteresis zone in volts.

examples.description: sets the height of the hysteresis zone to 27 mV.
might return TRIGger:HYSTeresis:USER:VALue 27.0e-3, indicating that the height of the hysteresis zone is 27 mV.

commands.shortDescription: This command sets or returns the height of the user-defined trigger hysteresis zone in volts.
commands.name: VALue

commands.description: This query-only command returns the current state of the triggering system.

examples.description: might return TRIGGER:STATE ARMED, indicating that the pretrigger data is being acquired.

commands.returns:
ARMED indicates that the instrument is acquiring pretrigger information.
AUTO indicates that the instrument is in the automatic mode and acquires data
even in the absence of a trigger.
READY indicates that all pretrigger information is acquired and that the instrument
is ready to accept a trigger.
SAVE indicates that the instrument is in save mode and is not acquiring data.
TRIGGER indicates that the instrument triggered and is acquiring the post trigger
information.
commands.shortDescription: This query-only command returns the current state of the triggering system.
commands.name: STATE
